entries.title: CLASE: Chinese LegAlese Stylistic Evaluation
entries.notes: Hybrid, reference-free evaluation of stylistic fidelity in Chinese legal text, combining linguistic features with experience-guided LLM-as-a-judge scoring; experiments on 200 legal documents.

entries.title: Towards Computational Chinese Paleography
entries.notes: Position paper charting the computational turn in Chinese paleography, from automating isolated visual tasks toward integrated, human-centric digital research ecosystems.

entries.title: Pun2Pun: Textual-Visual Chinese-English Pun Translation via Linguistic Reasoning
entries.notes: Benchmark for Chinese-English pun translation over text and images, with the Constant-Variable Optimization (CVO) translation strategy and the Overlap (Ovl) metric.

entries.title: Do Androids Question Electric Sheep? A Multi-Agent Simulation of Philosophical Reflection
entries.notes: Philosopher and Symposium frameworks simulate self- and group-reflection for multi-persona agents; identifies an "overthinking threshold" beyond which deliberation yields diminishing returns.

entries.title: PanelTR: Zero-Shot Table Reasoning Through Multi-Agent Discussion
entries.venue: International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
entries.notes: Five LLM scientist personas investigate, self-review, and peer-review their way through table QA and fact verification, outperforming vanilla LLMs and rivaling supervised models without task-specific training.

entries.title: Constituent Order Differences in Adverbials, in English and Chinese News
entries.notes: LLM-annotated comparable corpora show English news favors core-information-first narration with postposed adverbials, while Chinese news favors background-first presentation with preposed ones.
